subject: Configurable regional retention: deployment scope & timeline
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: legal@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Acme requirements: regional data retention and deletion needs

Hi Markus / Karthik,

Thanks for taking this call last week. Per our security and compliance review, Acme Health needs the following for any tenant that stores EU patient metadata: 

- Data residency: all processed tokens and derived embeddings for EU tenants must be stored in EU-only storage zones (no cross-region backups).
- Retention: default retention 7 years for PHI-adjacent artifacts, configurable per-tenant down to 90 days for non-PHI tenants.
- Deletion: ability to trigger immediate permanent purge (not soft-delete) plus audit log for erase operations.
- Legal hold: must be able to suspend deletion for a tenant with a legal-hold flag for up to 2 years.

I've attached a short matrix (acme_requirements.pdf) with examples. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports per-tenant storage selection and per-tenant retention configuration today, and if not, what the rough timeline and constraints would be?

We'd like a proposal for the deployment approach (hosted vs dedicated zone mapping), an estimate of engineering effort, and any compliance gaps you see.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

— Priya Shah
Director, IT Compliance
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_requirements.pdf (1 page)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme requirements: regional data retention and deletion needs

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear matrix. Looping in Karthik (product) and Laura (security program) to scope this.

Short answers up front:
- Per-tenant storage selection: not fully GA; we have regional routing and geofenced storage for dedicated tenants but need to expose per-tenant admin controls in the console and admin API.
- Per-tenant retention: we currently support workspace-level retention presets; fine-grained per-tenant TTLs with immediate purge and legal-hold interactions are not exposed yet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Clarify functional expectations: is the 7-year default a hard requirement for ALL EU tenants or only for tenants that will ingest PHI? (that affects scope)
2) Define the admin contract: console + admin API + audit logs + RBAC for triggering purges/legal-hold
3) Technical constraints: we need to decide whether to implement retention as a metadata TTL with region-aware garbage collection or as an offline purge job that touches cold backups.

I've attached an initial retention matrix (retention_matrix_v2.xlsx) that outlines field names we'd need in the admin API, proposed flags (region_zone, tenant_ttl_days, legal_hold_until), and a first-pass estimation of migration paths. Can you review and flag anything missing?

Proposed timeline (tentative):
- Product spec draft: 2 weeks (target 2028-03-19)
- Engineering spike & prototype: 2 sprints (~4 weeks)
- Canary deployment (one EU tenant): 8–10 weeks after spec sign-off

If this meets your needs, we can schedule a technical sync with your engineering security lead.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Forwarding Priya's asks — we need engineering feasibility and a prioritized list of what to build for configurable retention and region storage. Key questions I want a quick read on: 

- Storage model: can we guarantee that backups/snapshots also remain in-region for dedicated tenants?
- Admin API: what fields are non-negotiable for Acme (tenant_ttl_days, legal_hold_flag, region_zone)?
- Deletion semantics: do we offer immediate irreversible purge, or do we implement a two-step process (soft-delete -> permanent purge)?
- Auditability: what events do we log and for how long?

See the matrix Markus attached. Please reply inline with engineering constraints and a rough estimate (LOE) in story points or engineer-weeks.

Thanks — Karthik

Thanks for the heads up — quick engineering read: 

1) Storage / backups: For Dedicated tenants we can guarantee in-region storage for primary and snapshot volumes if the tenant is deployed to an EU cluster. For Hosted tenants we currently replicate cold backups to a single DR region (which could be outside EU) — to meet "no cross-region backups" we need to implement region-scoped archival buckets and change snapshot tooling (~3 weeks dev + 1 week ops runbook).

2) Retention model: Two feasible implementation paths: 
   a) TTL metadata + region-aware GC: attach tenant_ttl_days to every record and run a distributed GC that respects region_zone. Pros: immediate, constant-time checks; Cons: requires KV-store changes and careful coordination with inference cache. Estimated LOE: 3–4 engineer-sprints.
   b) Offline purge jobs: run scheduled purge jobs that delete data and then reconcile backups. Pros: simpler to implement; Cons: deletion may be nondeterministic latency up to 24–72 hours, which may not satisfy "immediate purge" requirement. Estimated LOE: 2 sprints.

3) Legal hold: we can add legal_hold_until on tenant metadata that prevents GC/purge. Need a retention-exempt marker for the archive process. Small implementation (1 sprint) plus audit-log extension (1 sprint).

4) Admin API & console: Admin API fields we need: tenant_id, region_zone, tenant_ttl_days (int), legal_hold_flag (bool), legal_hold_until (timestamp), purge_initiator (user_id), purge_type (soft|hard). Console changes: per-tenant retention panel + an audit view. Estimated LOE: 2 sprints backend + 1.5 sprints frontend.

5) Auditability: Log events for retention_change, purge_requested, purge_completed, legal_hold_set/cleared. Retain audit logs for 3 years by default; for Acme we can offer extended retention as part of enterprise agreement.

6) Migration & compatibility: We need a migration path for existing tenants (retroactively tag records with TTL or run a one-off archival job). Migration effort depends on dataset size; recommend a canary tenant for the first run.

Overall estimate (end-to-end product + infra + console + docs + runbooks): 8–10 sprints to full GA if prioritized. Can deliver a limited-scope canary (per-tenant TTL + in-region GC for active storage) in ~6 weeks (2 sprints spec + 2 sprints proto + 2 sprints canary).

I'll draft a short engineering plan and JIRA epics for RETAIN work.

— Monica Patel
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime

Hi Priya — thanks for the quick review and the team for the detailed read. Action items and proposed commitments below: 

Action items (owners):
- Product spec draft covering per-tenant retention API + console panel (Owner: me) — target 2028-03-19
- Engineering spike to validate in-region GC vs offline purge for active inference state (Owner: Monica) — deliverables: prototype + perf numbers (2 sprints)
- Backup retention change for dedicated tenants (Owner: Ops/Infra, cc Laura) — runbook + 3-week implementation window
- Audit log schema extension + retention policy (Owner: Security, cc Laura) — spec in 2 weeks
- Legal hold semantics doc + API contract (Owner: Monica + Legal) — draft for review in 2 weeks

Canaries and timeline:
- Canary: one EU non-PHI tenant fully on in-region active storage + TTL controls — target pilot start 2028-04-16
- GA: dependent on pilot results; provisional estimate +8–10 sprints from spec sign-off (see Monica's end-to-end estimate).

Related artifacts: JIRA: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RETAIN-123 (epic created), design draft in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-retention-specs

Priya — can you confirm two items so we can finalize the spec?
1) Is the 7-year retention a contractual minimum for any tenant that will ever process PHI, or should we only apply it to tenants explicitly flagged as "PHI-enabled"?
2) For backups: is an "in-region primary" + "in-region archival buckets" approach sufficient, or do you require zero cross-region copies under all failure scenarios?

If you prefer, we can set a 30-minute technical sync later this week to walk the proposed canary flow.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
